item.title: Western Romania: Church of Sântămăria Orlea on Europa Nostra list of most endangered heritage sites in Europe
item.description: The Reformed Church of Sântămăria Orlea, in western Romania’s Hunedoara county, is on Europa Nostra’s 2026 list of the 7 Most Endangered Heritage Sites in Europe. item.title: Romanian street cat wins European Feline Championship held in Austria
item.description: Duracell, a cat rescued from the streets of Iași, eastern Romania, has received the highest award at the European Feline Championship held in Graz, Austria. Rescued by Mihaela Merlă and Ionuț Proboteanu, the breeders of the 2025 World Champion, RO Bucovina Kira Kiralina, Duracell grew up alongside pedigree cats and participated in numerous international competitions. item.title: Bucharest’s main airport to install seven electric vehicle charging stations
item.description: The Henri Coandă International Airport, Bucharest’s main one, will install seven electric vehicle charging stations as part of a broader strategy to modernize infrastructure. The National Company Bucharest Airports (CNAB) has launched a public tender for the project. In a post on Facebook, Bucharest Airports announced that the seven charging stations will be located in North Parking - P7 at Henri Coandă International Airport. item.title: Donald Trump to reportedly be invited to Bucharest for B9 Summit
item.description: US president Donald Trump will be invited to attend the Bucharest Nine (B9) Summit scheduled for May 13 in Romania’s capital, according to political sources cited by Euronews Romania. The Romanian Presidency is set to send an official invitation to Washington, DC. Invitations will also be sent to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, according to the same source. item.title: Romanian tech group Simtel reports RON 600 mln in revenues in 2025
item.description: Engineering and technology group Simtel (BVB: SMTL), a company listed on the Main Market of the Bucharest Stock Exchange, reported consolidated preliminary operating revenues of RON 605.7 million (EUR 118.7 million) in 2025, up 68% compared to 2024 and approximately 20% above the budgeted level. Revenues from core operations amounted to RON 598.4 million, representing a 69% increase year-on-year. item.title: Romanian Court of Appeal upholds nine-month prison sentence for Wiz Khalifa
item.description: American rapper Wiz Khalifa is to serve a nine-month prison sentence in Romania after the Constanța Court of Appeal rejected his annulment appeal, issuing a final ruling in the case. The sentence stems from a 2024 incident in which the artist smoked cannabis on stage at a music festival in Costinești. item.title: EBRD cuts forecast for Romania’s economy to 1.2% growth this year, followed by 2.2% in 2027
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has reduced the forecast for the Romanian economy in 2026 to 1.2% growth, compared to 1.6% envisaged in September, under the Regional Economic Prospects report published on February 26. The country’s economy would accelerate to 2.2% in 2027, according to the bank’s scenario. item.title: Romania posts budget surplus in January as spending is restrained by lack of budget law
item.description: The general government budget execution data for January, not yet published officially but consulted by Ziarul Financiar, show a surplus of RON 845 million (over EUR 160 million, or 0.04% of GDP). The revenues of RON 55.1 billion were higher than the RON 54.3 billion expenses. item.title: Romania raises nearly EUR 1 bln with private placements in January-February
item.description: The Ministry of Finance of Romania has used the instrument of private placements, negotiated directly with the large banks, at lower interest rates, continuing the series of financings of this type used last year. In January, the ministry raised nearly EUR 1 billion with such instruments, on top of the EUR 3 billion and USD 2 billion of Eurobonds issued. item.title: Romania’s largest chemical producer Chimcomplex to cut 1,200 jobs, cites lack of state support
item.description: Chimcomplex, Romania’s largest chemical company and part of the CRC Group (BVB: CRC), will lay off 1,200 employees, shut down energy-intensive production lines, and expand its trading division, owner Ștefan Vuza announced in the company’s annual financial report.
